primaryKeyword: what is the salary of seo in india
h1: SEO salaries in India, by role and experience
metaTitle: What Is the Salary of SEO in India? 2026 Bands
metaDescription: What is the salary of SEO in India in 2026? Intern to head of SEO, with monthly and annual INR bands, city differences and what moves you up a band.
answer: SEO salaries in India run from about ₹20,000 a month for a trainee to ₹2,08,000–₹3,75,000 a month for a head of SEO. An executive with one to two years earns roughly ₹25,000–₹50,000 a month, a specialist ₹50,000–₹1,00,000, a manager ₹1,00,000–₹2,08,000. City and employer type move each band by 30% or more.
takeaways: Seven rungs, and the gap between the bottom and the top is roughly **15x**. Almost none of it is explained by years served.
Each jump is earned by a specific, nameable capability — not by tenure and not by a certificate.
**City still moves pay by 30–50%** for the same role. Remote hiring narrowed that gap; it hasn't closed it.
Product companies pay most, export-facing agencies next, domestic services agencies least — for identical work.

sections.h2: The full ladder, monthly and annual
body: Seven rungs cover almost every SEO job an Indian company actually posts. The bands are wide on purpose, because they genuinely are wide — the same title at a Bengaluru product company and an Indore services agency can differ by 3x.
These are market ranges we see in hiring and in client conversations, not survey data. Nobody publishes a reliable SEO salary census in India. Anyone quoting one to the rupee invented it.

callout.title: CTC is not take-home
callout.body: Indian offers are quoted as CTC, which already contains employer PF, gratuity and often a variable component you may or may not receive. Take-home typically lands 15–25% below the headline once PF, professional tax and income tax come out. Always ask for the fixed-versus-variable split before comparing two offers.

sections.h2: The capability that earns each jump
body: Every band above answers one question: what can this person be left alone with? Promotions in SEO follow the answer, not the calendar.
Nothing clever. Accuracy, deadlines, and not needing to be chased. A trainee who delivers 40 correctly optimised pages on the date promised gets confirmed; one who delivers 60 with errors doesn't.

subs.h3: Executive to Senior Executive — explaining why a number moved
body: The first real jump. You stop reporting what happened and start saying why. "Traffic is down 18%" is executive work. "Traffic is down 18% because 200 product pages lost internal links in the July release, here's the URL list" is the band above.
It's also where you learn to read Search Console rather than screenshot it. Filtering to the fifteen queries that make money, instead of a site-wide average, is a surprisingly rare skill.

subs.h3: Senior Executive to Specialist — owning one discipline unsupervised
body: Pick a lane and go deep enough that nobody reviews your work. Content and on-page is the crowded lane; technical is the better-paid one, which is why the two specialist rows above differ by nearly ₹10 lakh at the top end.

For the technical route, the capability that opens the door is answering "why isn't Google seeing this page?" from evidence — crawl data, rendered HTML, server logs. [Log file analysis](/glossary/log-file-analysis) is the single skill most likely to move someone into that band.

subs.h3: Specialist to Manager — writing and defending a plan
body: The jump from doing to deciding, and the largest pay step on the ladder. You put a quarter's plan in front of a founder, explain the trade-offs, and take the blame when a bet doesn't pay. Technical skill is assumed by now; the argument is what you're paid for. Managing people is often part of it but isn't what earns the band — plenty of managers manage nobody and are paid for owning the number.

subs.h3: Manager to Head of SEO — forecasting and budget defence
body: You're arguing for organic against paid in a meeting where somebody has to lose. That needs a forecast you'll be held to, a hiring plan, and a view on where search demand in your category goes over three years. Very few people can do this, which is why the band is what it is and why those roles stay open for months.

sections.h2: City multipliers: what the same role pays where
body: Location still moves Indian SEO pay by 30–50% for identical work. Remote hiring compressed it and didn't close it, because employers benchmark against local cost of living and — more importantly — against how many other employers are bidding for the same person.
Read the multipliers against the national mid-band for a role. A manager on a ₹12,00,000–₹25,00,000 band sits near the top of it in Bengaluru and near the bottom in Indore.

body: Employer type moves the number about as much as city does, and for a structural reason rather than a cultural one.
bullets: **Domestic services agency — lowest band.** Your salary is a slice of a retainer that also funds tools, management, four disciplines and margin. What you get instead is volume: fifteen sites and three migrations in two years, which is the fastest way to get genuinely good.

**Export-facing agency — 20–40% above domestic.** Revenue in dollars and pounds, competing globally for the same person. Also the usual training ground for anyone who later works remotely for overseas clients.
**In-house at a traditional business — mid-band.** Stable, slower, and often the most interesting technical problems, because the site is old and complicated.
**Product company, marketplace or funded startup — top band.** Benchmarked against engineering and product pay rather than agency margins.

**Founder or freelancer — no band at all.** Revenue, not salary, and a sales job with SEO delivery attached. [How much SEO pays across all four routes](/answers/how-much-does-seo-pay) compares them properly.

callout.title: The other side of these numbers
callout.body: If you're a founder reading this to plan a hire rather than a career, salary is only about 70% of the cost. Recruitment, equipment, insurance, tools and three to four months of ramp add the rest — [what it costs to hire SEO talent in India](/journal/what-it-costs-to-hire-seo-talent-in-india) does that arithmetic in full.

sections.h2: What AI skills do to your band
body: Two effects pulling in opposite directions, and which one you feel depends on the rung you're standing on.

Below the specialist band, AI compresses pay. The work that fills an executive's week — meta tags, keyword grouping, first drafts, report summaries — has a checkable right answer, which is exactly what software does well now. Fewer of those seats get funded, and the survivors expect more.
Above the specialist band, AI fluency adds to your band. Not because you can prompt a chatbot — everyone can — but because a small set of adjacent capabilities are now genuinely scarce.
bullets: **Building and auditing content pipelines.** Anyone can generate 200 pages. Few can build a process that keeps them accurate, differentiated and on the right side of Google's scaled-content line.

**Optimising for AI answers.** How brands get cited in AI Overviews and assistants is emerging and badly understood — [generative engine optimization](/glossary/generative-engine-optimization) is the label it's settling on, and early credible expertise is being paid for.

**Verification and editorial accountability.** In fintech, health and legal, the person who signs off that a draft is correct is now the expensive person in the room. A subject-matter skill, not a writing one.
**Data and scripting.** Search Console API, warehouse queries, automated crawl diffs. This always paid more; the gap just widened.

sections.h2: How to use these numbers without embarrassing yourself
body: **Ranges are ranges for a reason.** A ₹6,00,000–₹12,00,000 specialist band means the person at the top does measurably different work from the person at the bottom. Quoting the top of a band without evidence you belong there is how you lose the room. Bring what you moved, on which site, with before-and-after numbers you can explain from memory.

**Titles inflate fastest at the bottom.** "SEO Manager" on a three-year CV usually means managing a checklist, not a plan. If you're hiring, interview for what somebody decided, not what they did. If you're job-hunting, be honest with yourself about which one you've been doing.

**Aggregate salary sites over-report Indian marketing pay**, because self-reported data skews toward metros, larger employers and people happy enough with their number to submit it. Use them for shape, never for a target.

faqs.q: What is the salary of an SEO fresher in India?
faqs.a: Roughly ₹20,000–₹35,000 a month, or ₹2,40,000–₹4,20,000 a year, with internships paying ₹8,000–₹25,000 as a stipend. Metro product companies sit at the top of that; tier-2 services agencies at the bottom. It's a low band because the tasks are learnable in weeks and a lot of people have learned them.

faqs.q: What is an SEO executive's salary in India?
faqs.a: About ₹25,000–₹50,000 a month, or ₹3,00,000–₹6,00,000 a year, for one to two years of experience. The way out of that band is being able to explain why a number moved rather than just reporting that it did — that's what a senior executive or analyst role is actually paying for.

faqs.q: What is an SEO manager's salary in India?
faqs.a: Around ₹1,00,000–₹2,08,000 a month, or ₹12,00,000–₹25,00,000 a year, typically at five to eight years. Bengaluru, Gurugram and Mumbai sit at the top of the band and tier-2 cities 20–35% below. The band is paid for owning the plan and the number, not for years served.

faqs.q: Is SEO salary higher in Bengaluru than other Indian cities?
faqs.a: Yes — typically 15–35% above the national mid-band for the same role, with Delhi NCR just behind and Mumbai close after. It isn't about cost of living so much as competition: Bengaluru has the deepest pool of product companies and export-facing agencies bidding for the same shortlist.

faqs.q: Which SEO role pays the most in India?
faqs.a: Head of SEO or organic growth, at ₹25,00,000–₹45,00,000+ a year, followed by senior technical SEO at product companies, which can reach ₹22,00,000. Beyond salaried roles, remote work for US and UK clients pays more again, because it's priced against the client's market rather than yours.

faqs.q: How can I increase my SEO salary in India?
faqs.a: Pick one high-paying capability and become undeniable at it — technical debugging, data and scripting, or a regulated vertical like fintech or health. Then change what you're accountable for, not just where you work. Two lateral moves for a raise leave you with one year of experience repeated four times.
